rationale: All four lenses and the standards audit ran; 7 blocking findings: five approved-spec deviations from the acceptance audit (CR-003 pct formula and CR-004 started-log fields need a human decision; CR-001, CR-002, CR-005, CR-006 are mechanical), plus a missing end-to-end test of the real service-account scope allowlist (CR-007). 0 deferred (code-review-deferred.md holds only a no-deferred-items stub this subagent could not delete); 26 candidates dismissed after source checks, mostly spec-authorized behavior (scope lifts when disabled, partial failure leaves project/admins, cost center only when names differ, existing project's link kept, admin grant on existing shared projects) or disproved in code (soft_budget non-nullable, budget_reset_at is str, update applies 80% default for soft_budget None, 0.5 pct tolerance, detached project reads loaded columns only, anyio fixture present, logout is the only other provider call), plus the input-trimming standards finding and the float-overflow cap, both settled by the user's 2026-10-19 decisions (keep trimming; finite-only, no cap).

findings.title: Spec's get_active_by_emails not implemented
findings.problem: The approved spec (Resolution step 1; Components > Changed) requires a new UserRepository.get_active_by_emails(session, emails) -> dict[str, UserDB]. The diff instead adds an active_only flag to the existing get_by_emails, and _assign_admins and _list_projects_sync call get_by_emails(session, emails, active_only=True).
findings.impact: Behavior is equivalent today, but the repository API deviates from the approved design: the acceptance criterion for admin resolution and the repository component stay partial, and a shared method's contract gained a flag the spec did not approve.
findings.recommendation: Add UserRepository.get_active_by_emails(session, emails) -> dict[str, UserDB] (mirrors get_by_emails plus the is_active/deleted_at filter of get_active_by_id) and call it from ServiceNowIntegrationService._assign_admins and _list_projects_sync, per spec Resolution step 1 and Components > Changed; or record an approved spec amendment that keeps get_by_emails(active_only=True).

findings.title: Security module imported eagerly, spec requires lazy
findings.problem: Spec (Conventions > Imports; Scope restriction) requires the ServiceNow security module to be imported lazily inside authenticate(), matching the Teams resolver. authentication.py imports enforce_servicenow_scope and is_servicenow_service_account at module top level.
findings.impact: The approved wiring convention is not met (acceptance row fails). Every import of authentication.py now loads servicenow_access, and the module pair relies on servicenow_access's own lazy back-import to avoid a cycle, which the spec's lazy wiring was meant to avoid.
findings.recommendation: Move the servicenow_access import inside authenticate()'s external branch next to the Teams resolver import, and inside servicenow_integration_access_only, per spec Conventions > Imports and Scope restriction; keep servicenow_access's own lazy import of ACCESS_DENIED_MESSAGE.

findings.title: Pct math deviates from spec formula
findings.problem: Spec (Write step 3, amounts to payload) says non-platform pct = amount / total x 100 via unrounded Decimal and platform = 100 - sum(other pcts), so the percentages sum to exactly 100. build_category_specs instead computes every category, platform included, independently through _exact_pct, which walks neighbouring floats with math.nextafter so each derived amount matches the request exactly. The sum then equals 100 only within float noise, and the tests disagree on the guarantee: test_specs_cover_all_categories_and_sum_to_100 checks < 1e-9, while the derive-back test allows <= 0.5.
findings.impact: No live failure was found: project_budget_service accepts sums within PCT_SUM_TOLERANCE (0.5) and the drift is far below that. But the shipped algorithm differs from the approved design, and the two tests state conflicting guarantees, so a future tolerance change could start rejecting requests without a clear contract to test against.
findings.recommendation: Decide between (a) implementing the spec formula — non-platform pct = amount / total × 100 via unrounded Decimal, platform = 100 − sum(other pcts), so the pcts sum to exactly 100 — and (b) amending the spec to accept the current per-category exact-derivation search in _exact_pct. Then align test_specs_cover_all_categories_and_sum_to_100 (< 1e-9) and the derive-back test (<= 0.5 drift) on one stated guarantee.

findings.title: Started log lacks spec-required fields
findings.problem: Spec (Conventions > Logging) says both servicenow_budget_request_started and servicenow_budget_request_completed carry request_id, action, project, cost_center, created_project, created_cost_center, admins_assigned/admins_pending counts and actor_user_id. The started log carries request_id, action, project, epam_project_code, an admin_emails count and actor_user_id; cost_center, created_* and the assigned/pending counts are not known until the request has run.
findings.impact: The logging criterion stays partial, and the spec as written cannot be met literally, so the fix depends on which reading the author intended. Operators correlating started/completed lines get different field sets.
findings.recommendation: Decide what servicenow_budget_request_started must carry: spec Conventions > Logging asks for cost_center, created_project, created_cost_center and admins_assigned/admins_pending counts, which are unknown before the request runs. Either log request-derived equivalents under those names, or amend the spec so those fields are required on the completed log only (which already carries all of them).

findings.title: Check phase skips get_project_budget_group
findings.problem: Spec (Write step 3) says the check phase reads the current group with project_budget_group_repository.get_active_by_project and project_budget_service.get_project_budget_group. _read_group/_read_budgets instead read category budgets through project_budget_assignment_repository.get_active_by_group_id + budget_repository.get_by_ids, with their own active/deleted filtering, and a test asserts get_project_budget_group is not awaited. The _create_group conflict re-read uses the same path.
findings.impact: The integration computes merge/replace amounts and preserved soft limits from a hand-rolled read that duplicates the budget service's group-loading rules instead of the approved service call, so the two can drift (e.g. which budgets count as active) and the UI and ServiceNow would then see different current amounts.
findings.recommendation: Read the current group in the check phase through project_budget_group_repository.get_active_by_project plus project_budget_service.get_project_budget_group as spec Write step 3 states (and in the _create_group conflict re-read), then update the test that asserts get_project_budget_group is not awaited; or record an approved spec amendment for the repository-based _read_budgets.

findings.title: list_projects lacks 'caller must authorize' docstring
findings.problem: Spec (Components) requires new methods that skip permission checks to say so in their docstrings ("caller must authorize"). ServiceNowIntegrationService.list_projects performs no authorization and has no docstring; apply_budget_request, create_shared_project_in_session and get_or_create do carry it.
findings.impact: A future caller can reuse list_projects from a less-guarded route without any marker that authorization is the caller's job, exposing which shared projects arbitrary emails belong to.
findings.recommendation: Add a docstring to ServiceNowIntegrationService.list_projects stating that it performs no permission check ("Caller must authorize."), per spec Components.

findings.title: No end-to-end test of real scope allowlist
findings.problem: No test sends a routed request through the real authenticate for the ServiceNow service account. The router tests' http fixture sets app.dependency_overrides[authenticate], so enforce_servicenow_scope never runs there. TestAuthenticateServiceNowScope and TestEnforceServiceNowScope patch _allowed_routes to a fixed set and use hand-built route objects, and TestAllowlistMatchesRouter only compares _allowed_routes() with a hard-coded set. The allow side, where FastAPI fills scope['route'] and the included route path matches the module router's path, is never exercised. Gap shape: regression-gap; evidence: router test fixture override and patched allowlist in the security tests.
findings.impact: Consumer: ServiceNow service-account calls to list_servicenow_projects and apply_servicenow_budget through app.include_router at main.py:1114. The code is correct today (the router is included with no extra prefix), but if routing and the allowlist stop lining up (an added prefix, a sub-app mount, a FastAPI change in when scope['route'] is set), the check fails closed, the service account gets 403 on its own two endpoints and the whole integration breaks with no failing test.
findings.recommendation: Add an HTTP test that runs the real authenticate (patch get_user_provider / IdpFactory instead of overriding authenticate) on an app that includes servicenow_integration.router, and assert the ServiceNow service account gets 200 on GET /v1/integrations/servicenow/projects and POST /v1/integrations/servicenow/budgets and 403 on a non-integration route registered on the same app.
